quote: Well, I do have a solar,
stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing solar-linked program (Sacred Power) but the rep never asks what company, what was installed, or what happened to it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have been deliberately avoiding scope creep by not engaging further, but nothing in the transcript suggests a strategic hold — the rep simply misreads the answer as being about a literal appliance.
coaching_implication: When a customer references a prior solar program by name, the rep should ask a clarifying follow-up (which company, is it still active, what happened) before concluding the call doesn't fit.

quote: You were looking for a solar refrigerator?
stewart_read: Rep takes the customer's rambling, likely-mistranslated request literally instead of recognizing this is probably a confused description of an existing program's promised appliance replacement.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer may in fact be asking about a literal solar-powered refrigerator, in which case the rep's read is correct and the DQ is clean — but the corroded-refrigerator complaint context suggests a warranty/service issue tied to a prior solar deal, not a new purchase interest.
coaching_implication: Rep should slow down and ask one more clarifying question — 'is this a system you already have installed?' — before disengaging.

quote: I'll give you off our list, though, but you have a good rest of your day.
stewart_read: The call ends with no button-up, no next step owned by the rep, and no attempt to confirm whether this is a genuine DQ or a misrouted/confused lead.
coaching_implication: Even on a non-standard call, rep should confirm understanding before removing someone from the list — a quick clarifying question could reveal a real solar lead underneath the confusing wording.

quote: I think I found it here. So it's just a single family home?
stewart_read: Nearly a minute and a half is spent trying to locate the customer's address on a map before basic qualification can proceed, a significant efficiency drag this early in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be unavoidable system/mapping friction rather than a rep skill gap, since the rep explicitly says the pin is wrong on the map.
coaching_implication: When address lookup fails, rep should verbally confirm city/state and move on to qualification rather than spending visible dead air resolving the map pin.

quote: I have you, Cecilia, down as the property owner. Is there anybody else in the title of the home with you?
stewart_read: Rep runs the co-owner check correctly and moves on cleanly when the customer says no.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here — this segment was handled to standard.
